description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mark Esper, former U.S. Secretary of Defense under the first Trump administration, says drones and sea mines remain the most complicated threats in the Strait of Hormuz and could delay US naval escort missions. Bob McNally, founder and president of Rapidan Energy Group, says oil markets could face weeks of disruption based on current conditions in the Strait. US Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum says the Trump administration is taking steps to increase US energy production amid the war in Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Judge Blocks Subpoenas Against Fed Chair Powell | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/13/2026

author: Andreina Itriago, Chris Strohm, Ben Bartenstein
description: The Trump administration is working with Venezuela’s interim government to bring a key ally of ousted leader Nicolás Maduro to the US to face prosecution on charges that could include money laundering, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Venezuela Officials in Talks to Send Detained Maduro Ally to US

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Friday signed an agreement finalizing a trade deal with Ecuador, reducing tariff rates on a number of goods traded between the two economies.
title: Trump Administration Finalizes Ecuador Trade Deal to Cut Tariffs

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: The US is slated to receive around $10 billion as a fee from investors as part of the recently completed deal for China’s ByteDance Ltd. to sell the American operations of the social video app TikTok to a consortium of US investors, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
title: US to Receive $10 Billion Fee for TikTok Deal, WSJ Reports

author: Molly Schuetz, Jeff Mason
description: Richard Grenell was replaced as head of the John F. Kennedy Center after a tumultuous year that saw many artists and groups cancel shows at one of the nation’s most prestigious performing arts institutions.
title: Kennedy Center Chief Replaced After Wave of Artist Cancellations

description: Bob McNally, founder and president of Rapidan Energy Group and Former Special Assistant and Senior Director for International Energy on the National Security Council under President George W. Bush, says oil markets could face weeks of disruption based on current conditions in the Strait. McNally says the Hormuz artery is "too big and important," downplaying the impact the IEA's largest-ever emergency oil release will have on markets. He expects oil prices will stay in the triple digit range until a ceasefire is reached. He speaks on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: McNally: Oil Disruption From Hormuz Could Last Weeks

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Tyler Kendall, Isis Almeida
description: The Trump administration has discussed trading in the oil futures market as a strategy to help curb surging crude prices amid the war in Iran, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said.
title: US Officials Have Discussed Trading Oil Futures, Burgum Says

description: Mark Esper, former U.S. Secretary of Defense under the first Trump administration, says drones and sea mines remain the most complicated threats in the Strait of Hormuz and could delay US naval escort missions. Esper also reflects on the tragedy of recent US service member deaths in the Middle East. He speaks on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Esper: Drones, Mines Complicate Strait Escort Mission

description: US Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum says the Trump administration is taking steps to increase US energy production amid the war in Iran. He speaks on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Holding World Economy Hostage, Interior Sec. Burgum Says

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: On today’s Big Take podcast: Digital services have become the fastest-growing segment of international trade — in part because they’re unencumbered by global tariffs. Until now.
title: The Growing Push to Tax the Digital Economy

author: Catherine Lucey, Ari Natter
description: The Trump administration on Friday took action to clear the way for oil production off the California coast in a bid to ease the global fuel pressures created by the war with Iran.
title: Trump Officials Direct Sable to Resume California Oil Operations

author: Pat Rizzuto
description: The EPA Friday issued a revised air emissions rule for facilities that use ethylene oxide to sterilize medical equipment, medicines, spices, dried foods, and certain other products.
title: Trump’s EPA Eases Controls in Proposed Ethylene Oxide Rule

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: Top officials from US and China are set to meet this weekend to prepare.
title: Amid Iran War, Trump Administration Turns Toward Beijing Summit

description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman, a City University of New York professor, reacts to a federal judge's ruling that blocks a federal investigation of Fed Chair Powell. Krugman says President Trump and US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro are "harassing" Powell. Krugman says the independence of the Fed is on the line. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Krugman Says Pirro Is Harassing Fed Chair Powell

description: US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro rails against a federal judge's decision to block a federal probe into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. She says "no one is above the law" and her office will appeal the ruling.  She says "this is wrong and without legal authority." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Attorney Pirro Says Powell Is Not Above the Law

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg's Mike McKee about the fed's preferred inflation gauge and the economic impact of the Iran war on the US economy. Then, Mike Collins, managing director at PGIM Fixed Income, on the state of the bond market and the current private credit landscape. Plus, Kyivstar Group president and CEO Oleksandr Komarov joins the show from Kyiv to talk earnings from Ukraine's largest telecommunications company and providing services to a country at war. Finally, Bloomberg's Katrina Manson breaks down how the US military enlisted silicon valley to build up its AI warfare. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Economic Outlook Dragged Down by Iran War | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/13/2026

author: Courtney Subramanian, Katy O'Donnell
description: President Donald Trump signed two executive orders on Friday aimed at making homeownership more affordable, the latest step by the administration to ease cost-of-living concerns as the Iran conflict drives up gas prices and rattles markets.
title: Trump Signs Orders Aimed at Easing Mortgage Access, Home Costs

author: Myles Miller
description: The man who rammed his vehicle into a Detroit-area synagogue on Thursday, setting off a fire and an exchange of gunfire that left him dead, was interviewed by federal law enforcement years before the attack, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: US Agents Questioned Michigan Synagogue Attack Suspect in 2019

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall discuss the latest from the Trump Administration. On today's show, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck Partner Rosemary Becchi and Andesite CEO Brian Carbaugh. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Warns of New Strikes on Iran | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/13/2026

author: Alicia A. Caldwell, Myles Miller, Nacha Cattan
description: A massive warehouse on Salt Lake City’s west side has been purchased by the Department of Homeland Security, adding to a growing portfolio of industrial buildings the federal government is acquiring to expand immigration detention capacity.
title: DHS Buys Massive Warehouse in Salt Lake City to Detain Migrants

author: Jen Judson
description: The US Army has sent 10,000 interceptor drones developed in Ukraine to the Middle East as it looks to repel Iranian attacks without using up high-cost missile defenses, according to US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll.
title: US Sends Intercept Drones Used in Ukraine to Blunt Iran Strikes

author: Daniela Milanese, Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil’s government withdrew a visa previously granted to a US official who’d planned to travel to the South American country next week, a day after a judge barred him from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro during the trip.
title: Brazil Revokes Visa of US Official Who Sought to Meet Bolsonaro

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Catherine Lucey
description: The US said it had stepped up strikes on Iran to unprecedented levels as both sides in the war threatened to escalate a conflict hitting its two-week mark and upending energy flows and global financial markets.
title: US Intensifies Strikes, Rhetoric in Iran War as Oil Rises

author: Sanne Wass
description: Greenland’s representative in high-stakes diplomatic talks with the US over the Arctic territory is stepping down as foreign minister.
title: Greenland’s Top Diplomat Managing US Talks Steps Down

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said the US has Iranians who are residing in the country “under watch” amid new concerns about the potential for domestic terrorism during the war with Iran.
title: Trump Says Iranians in US Are ‘Under Watch’ Over Terrorism Fears

author: Martha Viotti Beck, Rachel Gamarski
description: A majority of Brazil’s Supreme Court justices have voted to keep Daniel Vorcaro in prison, maintaining pressure on Banco Master SA’s former chief executive officer to pursue a plea bargain that has unsettled the country’s political and judicial elite.
title: Brazil Top Court Keeps Banco Master’s Ex-CEO in Jail For Now

author: Jasmina Kuzmanovic, Jorge Valero
description: The European Union is close to overcoming a unique obstacle to Montenegro’s membership bid — the country’s de-facto use of the euro — people familiar with the matter said.
title: EU Floats Fix for Euro Use That’s Clouding Montenegro Membership

description: The US says expect another day of intense strike on Iran as the Trump administration comes under more pressure with oil prices hovering near $100 a barrel. Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Says Intense Strikes on Iran Will Continue With Oil Around $100

author: Martha Viotti Beck, Rachel Gamarski
description: Brazil’s Supreme Court is debating whether to release Daniel Vorcaro from jail, a move that would ease pressure on Banco Master SA’s former chief executive officer to pursue a plea bargain that has unsettled the country’s political and judicial elite.
title: Brazil Top Court Debates Release of Banco Master’s Ex-CEO With Plea Deal at Stake

author: Gerry Doyle
description: Mining the Strait of Hormuz would effectively render the narrow sea corridor impassable for escorts and tankers from any nation — including Iran’s own —  while removing the explosives can’t be done so long as Iran can attack the mine-sweeping ships.
title: Mines Across Hormuz Would Create Lethal Barrier to All Traffic

author: Fiona MacDonald
description: Within the span of a few hours on Thursday, Iran’s new Supreme Leader said he’d keep one of the world’s most important energy chokepoints closed and its head of national security said the country could plunge the whole Middle East into darkness, and hunt down US troops “running for safety.”
title: Iran’s Leaders Defy Trump With Bellicose Talk and Public Parades

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright
description: Switzerland’s government said stable relations with the European Union are a “strategic necessity” as it pushes to sell the public on the importance of closer ties with the bloc before a national vote on an accord.
title: Swiss Government Pushes EU Deal as a ‘Strategic Necessity’

description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Iran’s new leader Mojtaba Khamenei has been wounded as part of the US and Israeli campaign against the country. 
“We know the new so-called, not-so-supreme leader is wounded and likely disfigured,” Hegseth told a press conference. He said the US was “on plan to defeat, destroy, disable all of their meaningful military capabilities at a pace the world has never seen before.” he spoke at a pentagon press briefing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran's Supreme Leader Wounded, Likely Disfigured Says Hegseth (Full Presser)

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer called on companies seeking refunds for the almost $170 billion in tariffs overturned by the Supreme Court to give any money they receive back to their workers.
title: Tariff Refunds Should Go to US Workers as Bonuses, Greer Says

author: Olivia Fletcher
description: The UK and Ireland signed a renewed joint defense pact, as the neighboring nations bolster their security ties in an increasingly tense geopolitical landscape.
title: UK, Ireland Renew Defense Pact in Bid to Boost Security Ties

description: Iran’s new supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, is wounded and likely disfigured, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says during a press conference Friday at the Pentagon. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran’s Khamenei Wounded, Likely Disfigured, Hegseth Says

author: Roxana Tiron, Anthony Capaccio
description: US Central Command has assigned investigators to look into an attack on an all-girls elementary school in Iran that killed about 180 people, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said.
title: US Investigating Attack on Iranian Girls School, Hegseth Says

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the administration is seeking to maintain steady relations with China ahead of a high-level meeting this weekend that will set the stage for a summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.
title: Greer Says US Seeks Stability in China Ties Ahead of Paris Talks

author: Anthony Capaccio, Roxana Tiron
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Iran’s new leader Mojtaba Khamenei has been wounded as part of the US and Israeli campaign against the country.
title: Hegseth Says Khamenei ‘Wounded,’ ‘Likely Disfigured’

author: Robert Tuttle
description: The war in Iran has ended Canadian drivers’ nearly yearlong sojourn with lower gasoline prices ever since Prime Minister Mark Carney eliminated the country’s consumer carbon tax.
title: Canadian Drivers’ Reprieve from Carbon Tax Wiped Out by Iran War

author: Jim Wyss, Stephen Wicary
description: Cuba’s government confirmed it is talking with US officials as Donald Trump uses economic pressure to bring about change in the one-party state 90 miles off the coast of Florida.
title: Cuba Confirms Talks With US as Trump Pushes Island to Brink

description:
Chen Zhi, the tycoon who led a secret life as an alleged scam kingpin, was nabbed in Cambodia in January.

He is said to have run scam centers that stole billions from victims worldwide. Bloomberg looks at how things unraveled for the alleged ringleader. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Behind The Dramatic Capture of an Alleged Scam Kingpin

description: Young male voters are abandoning Trump. Bloomberg Opinion columnist David M. Drucker explains why. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Young Men That Have Abandoned Trump

author: Alberto Nardelli, Alex Wickham
description: America’s allies are increasingly anxious about the US president’s escalating campaign in the Middle East.
title: Trump Flatterers Privately Fuming at Iran War

author: Charlotte Hughes-Morgan
description: Dutch police arrested four men after an explosive device went off at a Rotterdam synagogue early Friday, the latest in a string of attacks on synagogues in Europe and the US.
title: Dutch Police Arrest Four Men After Rotterdam Synagogue Explosion

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Firat Kozok
description: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization intercepted an Iranian missile that entered Turkish airspace on Friday, Turkey’s Defense Ministry said in a statement.
title: NATO Intercepts Iranian Missile in Turkish Airspace

description:
"If [Trump] was looking for a quick political uprising in Iran, it's not happening."

American-Iranian author Vali Nasr tells Mishal Husain why the US and Israel can't count on a swift collapse of the Islamic regime. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why President Trump Can’t Bank on an Uprising in Iran

author: Andreo Calonzo
description: The Philippine military said US defense assets have stayed put in the Southeast Asian nation amid concerns that America may be shifting more firepower to the Middle East as the Iran war shows no signs of abating.
title: Philippines Sees No Pullout of US Military Assets Amid Iran War

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche expressed concern that temporary US authorization for Russian oil sales will help President Vladimir Putin fund his war on Ukraine.
title: Germany Concerned Russian Oil Sales Will Help Fund Putin’s War

author: Augusta Saraiva, Beatriz Reis
description: The growing religious zeal of young voters is poised to shape elections in Latin America’s largest country.
title: Insta-Savvy Churches Are Propelling Brazil’s Gen Z to the Right

author: Augusta Saraiva, Beatriz Reis
description: El creciente fervor religioso de los votantes jóvenes está a punto de marcar las elecciones en la economía más grande de América Latina.
title: Iglesias “instagrameables” empujan el voto de la generación Z de Brasil a la derecha

author: Yian Lee
description: China called on the US to stop selling weapons to Taiwan after a report that President Donald Trump could sign off on a $14 billion deal after his trip to Beijing later this month.
title: China Urges US to Stop Taiwan Arms Sales After New Deal Report

author: Maciej Martewicz
description: Poland’s defense minister insisted on Friday the government was still going to use €43.7 billion ($50.3 billion) from the European Union’s loans-for-weapons program despite a presidential veto.
title: Poland Says It Still Plans to Tap EU Defense Loans Despite Veto

author: Misha Savic
description: President Aleksandar Vucic said Serbia bought supersonic, air-to-surface missiles from China as part of $17 billion defense upgrades against what he claimed were hostile intentions of nearby NATO countries.
title: Serbia Buys Chinese Supersonic Missiles as Vucic Alleges Threats

description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy is set to meet French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris. The visit comes at a time where Ukraine risks facing depleted air defenses as the US-led war with Iran burns through global stockpiles of Patriot missiles, the most valuable weapon Kyiv has in its arsenal against relentless Russian attacks. Bloomberg's Greg Sullivan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Zelenskiy in Paris as Ukraine Faces Air Defense Squeeze

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, US President Donald Trump issued a new threat to Tehran, warning “watch what happens” today on Truth Social. Trump earlier said curbing Iran’s nuclear threat outweighs oil costs.

Iran’s new supreme leader said the Strait of Hormuz should remain shut and Tehran will look to open other fronts in the war if the US and Israel persist with their attacks. 

The US has issued its second authorization for buyers to take Russian oil cargoes already at sea to ease pressure on prices as the war in the Middle East continues.

Today's guest: Marija Veitmane, Head of Equity Research at State Street Global Markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Warns 'Watch What Happens' & US Allows Russian Oil Sales | Daybreak Europe 3/13/2026

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Sales of offline communication gear and paper maps surged in Moscow as residents adapt to repeated mobile internet disruptions in Russia’s capital.
title: Moscow’s Internet Outages Drive Sales of Pagers and Paper Maps

author: Kateryna Kadabashy, Patrick Sykes
description: US President Donald Trump threatened Iran with further attacks after the Islamic Republic’s new leader signaled defiance and suggested there would be no easing of a war that’s upending energy flows and global markets.
title: Trump Warns Iran to Watch What Happens as War Hits Two-Week Mark

description: The US issued its second authorization for buyers to take Russian oil cargoes already at sea, widening a temporary waiver given last week to India alone in an effort to ease pressure on prices. The latest measure applies to oil loaded before March 12 and runs for a month — limiting the number of vessels that can reach major buyers in time. Bloomberg’s Anthony di Paola reports.
title: US Issues License Authorizing Sale of Some Russian Oil

description: US President Donald Trump and Iran’s new supreme leader both struck defiant tones as the war in the Middle East continues. Mojtaba Khamenei said the Islamic Republic would seek to ensure the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed and added that Tehran would look to open other fronts in the war if the US and Israel persist with their attacks. The American president said in a social media post Thursday that preventing Iran from having nuclear weapons and threatening the Middle East is “of far
title: War Shows No Signs of Easing, Leaders Use Defiant Tones

description: Buildings and vehicles destroyed following airstrikes in Tehran, on March 12.
title: Strikes Continue as Hormuz Threat Keeps Oil on Edge

description: Iranian-American scholar Vali Nasr tells Mishal Husain why Iran isn’t breaking under the US-Israel bombing campaign, and the reasons behind Tehran’s belief that time is on its side. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why Iran’s New Leadership Is Betting on Endurance

author: Samy Adghirni, Claudia Cohen, Albertina Torsoli
description: Marine Le Pen’s push to make France’s far right palatable to the country’s corporate and old-money elite is stirring tensions inside her party as it edges closer than ever to the presidency.
title: Le Pen Courts France’s Elite, Rattling the Far Right’s Old Guard

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Dan Strumpf, Asantha Sirimanne
description: A deadly US torpedo strike has sparked an outcry in India, fraying the trust of a key security partner in Asia.
title: Killing of Modi’s Invited Iranian Guests Strains US-India Ties

author: Lucille Liu, Daniel Flatley
description: The framework for US President Donald Trump’s summit with China’s Xi Jinping is set to be hashed out this weekend as negotiators meet to discuss thorny issues such as tariffs, fentanyl and Taiwan.
title: Trump-Xi Agenda to Be Mapped Out as Negotiators Meet in Paris

author: Francesca Stevens
description: Vietnam’s police launched criminal proceedings into prominent journalist and blogger Le Anh Hung for alleged anti-state activities in a country where authorities maintain a tightly controlled media environment.
title: Vietnam Police Probe Prominent Journalist Over ‘Anti-State’ Acts

author: Yian Lee
description: Taiwan has received an invitation from Eswatini for President Lai Ching-te to attend celebrations marking King Mswati III’s birthday and coronation anniversary, a potential overseas trip that would be Lai’s first in more than a year.
title: Taiwan’s Lai May End Overseas Travel Drought With Trip to Africa’s Last Absolute Monarchy

author: Neil Jerome Morales
description: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations should position itself as a safe haven for investment amid worsening global volatility, the host country said.
title: Philippines Calls on Asean to Anchor Investment Certainty

author: Claire Jiao
description: Afghanistan said at least four people were killed in Pakistani strikes on the capital and other provinces.
title: Afghanistan Says Pakistan Strike on Kabul Leaves Four Dead

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: Japan and other Asia-Pacific nations are set to unveil at least $30 billion worth of agreements with US companies this weekend, as Trump administration officials descend on Tokyo to press for more collaboration with regional allies on energy and critical minerals.
title: Asia Set to Pledge $30 Billion in Energy, Mineral Deals With US

author: Eric Martin
description: President Donald Trump saw his capture of Venezuela’s Nicolas Maduro as a quick, clean operation that couldn’t have gone better. Half a world away in Iran, what he hoped would be another fast campaign has devolved into something far more complicated.
title: Trump’s Plan for Cuba Would Make the US the Island’s Patron

author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump’s administration began its second tariff investigation in as many days, continuing its effort to rebuild his key trade policy that was struck down by the Supreme Court.
title: US Starts Second Trade Probe in Trump’s Tariff Policy Revival

author: Sakura Murakami
description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi canceled her participation in some official events Thursday after developing cold-like symptoms, days before she’s scheduled to depart for a trip to the US to meet with President Donald Trump.
title: Takaichi Misses Events Due to Cold Symptoms Before Trump Visit

author: Jon Herskovitz, Chris Gallagher
description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he discussed the “serious situation in the region” with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as New Delhi looks for ways to secure the safe passage of tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Modi Talks With Iran’s President as Tankers Stall in Hormuz

author: Stephen Wicary
description: Cuba vowed to free dozens of prisoners as its president prepared to speak to the press for second time since Donald Trump cut off vital fuel supplies to the communist-run island after capturing its principal ally.
title: Cuba to Free 51 Prisoners, President to Speak Amid US Tension

description: From London to Mumbai, travelers are facing record fares and cancellations. The biggest aviation shock since the pandemic has erased 10% of global capacity, sending prices soaring. K. Oanh Ha explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Global Travel Hit by Soaring Air Fares

author: Derek Wallbank, Daniel Flatley
description: The US has issued its second authorization for buyers to take Russian oil cargoes already at sea, a move intended to ease growing pressure on prices as the war in the Middle East continues.
title: US Treasury Gives Green Light for Sale of More Russian Oil

author: Joe Mayes
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves and Energy Secretary Ed Miliband urged petrol retailers and energy suppliers to show restraint on price hikes as the UK’s Labour government tries to show voters it is taking action to limit economic pain resulting from the Iran war.
title: UK Urges Fuel Bosses to Limit Petrol Price Hikes Amid Iran War
